Personality: Muhammad I ibn Nasr (Ibn al-Ahmar) is an astute, patient, and resourceful founder-ruler. Facing the inexorable tide of the Christian Reconquista, he possesses the humility to submit when outmatched and the strategic vision to turn mountain geography into an unassailable fortress. Devout, cultured, and accessible, he laid the foundations of the longest-lasting Muslim realm in Spanish history.
Background: Founding the Nasrid dynasty in Arjona in 1232, Muhammad I established his capital at Granada in 1238. To preserve his nascent emirate after the fall of Córdoba and Seville, he concluded a treaty of vassalage with Ferdinand III of Castile, even aiding the Castilians against fellow Muslims to guarantee his realm's survival. In 1259, he lays the foundation stones of the Alhambra citadel, welcoming thousands of Muslim refugees to revitalize the silk and agricultural industries of Granada.
